note: #1950: the first hostile cases. Each case is several scripted Souls on one fresh world, scripted through the served eden.mjs (no model); every step is a check, and a case passes only when every check of every Soul held. A failed case is a finding for a new issue, never a reason to change its bar here.

items.bar: A Soul claimed from a second folder is refused soul.held-elsewhere; --move hands it over once; the first folder's next command reports the move.
The world restarts during a two-minute act; within 60 s of the restart the act's receipt reaches an end state and the Soul's next act is accepted. Two Souls, both in a two-minute act.

#1974 A1. One Soul sends 200 acts in 10 s through the launcher (eden.mjs, through its serve). Every act over its limits gets a 429 and none a 5xx: no answer to the flood is a 5xx, and at most 60 (the world's act limit a minute) are anything but 429. Three bystanders act every 2 s; each one's median act verdict time during the flood (POST /v1/edge/act in its own client trace) is within 1.5 times its own median over the 30 s before.

#1974 A2. Twelve Souls' serves reach the world through one relay. Each starts a 4 s rest; the relay cuts every stream at once and turns reconnects away for 6 s, so the rests end while the streams are down. Within 10 s of the relay reopening, every Soul's local copy (world-live.json) has been received again and its check hash equals the hash of the world's own live picture.

#1974 A3. Four Souls walk from where they arrive to the bandstand; once they are moving, a god (eden-god.mjs, dev:admin) places a 30 m garden wall, 2 m high, 8 m ahead of them across their heading. Within 90 s of the wall each walk has ended or been refused with a reason (its receipt in an end state; a reason or code unless it completed), and each Soul's next walk (to the fire circle) is accepted and moves it 1 m within 30 s. The report gives how long each Soul was held after the wall.
